reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a Fortnite gift-card redemption tutorial showing sign-in, code entry, and the Epic Games redemption page. The giveaway requests ordinary engagement such as likes, subscriptions, and comments, while the described evidence shows no payment request, creator credential request, impersonation claim, or deceptive transaction outcome.

citations.quote: I'm going to show you how to go ahead and redeem your Fortnite gift cards
You'll need to go ahead and sign in.
So here we want to go ahead and redeem the code so you'll put those 16. Characters in here.
And then the $10 is added to my account
I won't redeem this one. I'll leave this one for you guys.

opening.argument: The video ties a promised Fortnite gift card directly to audience actions, making the giveaway itself the solicitation. Viewers are told to reach a like threshold, identify themselves on social media, subscribe, and comment to qualify for a valuable digital reward. That is not merely a redemption lesson: it creates a low-effort path from engagement to a promised asset, while the creator controls both the selection and delivery of the prize. The instructional material gives the promotion credibility, but the central incentive remains: perform the requested actions and a gift card may be provided.

citations.quote: when we get 500 likes, go ahead and just tag me in some social media. Let me know and I'll come back here and I'll drop a gift card for you guys in the comments.
Once we hit 500 likes, I'll give a card away to somebody. Subscribed and commenting in the comments.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense establishes that a redemption page was shown, but that does not answer the separate promise-action relationship. Showing how a code works does not verify that the engagement-based giveaway will occur, who will receive it, or whether the stated conditions are meaningful. Its emphasis on no payment and no credential request also overlooks that the requested consideration here is likes, subscription, comments, and social-media contact.

citations.quote: when we get 500 likes, go ahead and just tag me in some social media.
Once we hit 500 likes, I'll give a card away to somebody.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted conditions describe ordinary promotional engagement, not proof of deception. The video also demonstrates the actual operational process and says the displayed card is being left for viewers rather than demanding payment or account credentials. The wrong-side argument shows only that a giveaway is conditional; it does not show that the reward is fabricated, that anyone lost money, or that the redemption process is fraudulent.

citations.quote: You'll need to go ahead and sign in.
And then the $10 is added to my account

opening.argument: Several risk signals converge around a valuable digital asset: the video exposes a gift-card code on the redemption page, directs viewers to an external redemption link, and presents the code as something viewers can claim while also pushing engagement. The screen shows a reward-redemption form with the code entered, and the narration says the card will be left for viewers. That combination can create urgency and competition around a scarce, easy-to-obtain game asset, while the audience is encouraged to act before someone else uses it. The evidence does not establish that every viewer can successfully redeem it or that the promised additional card will materialize.

Epic Redeem Link: https://www.epicgames.com/fortnite/en-US/vbuckscard
I'll leave this one for you guys.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the visible redemption workflow as reassurance, but a working-looking form and an asserted account credit do not prove that the publicly exposed opportunity is available to viewers or that the follow-up giveaway will be honored. The external link and displayed code amplify the pressure to act immediately, while the defense supplies no evidence about availability, eligibility, or the promised second card.

citations.quote: This video also contains Fortnite Gift Card Codes and with 500 likes another will be given out in the comments!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals are ordinary features of giving away a game card and explaining its official redemption route. The visual citation does not prove that the code was deceptive or that viewers were harmed, and the description identifies the Epic redeem link rather than a fabricated payment destination. The wrong-side case relies on uncertainty about future availability, not evidence that the shown redemption failed or that the reward was false.

And then the $10 is added to my account

opening.argument: Although presented as a technical tutorial, the video functions substantially as a promotion for the creator's audience channels. The redemption explanation is used to keep viewers engaged with a giveaway, direct them to social-media interaction, and encourage subscription and comments; the description also places the gift-card promise alongside creator and streaming links. The operational demonstration therefore serves as credibility-building around a participation funnel. A tutorial can be accurate in its narrow instructions while still using a promised game asset to steer viewers toward the creator's ecosystem.

make sure you stop in on my mixer account.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels the content by its instructional mechanics, but that is too narrow: the creator himself links the tutorial to subscriptions, comments, social-media tagging, and a separate streaming account. Those calls to action are not required to redeem a Fortnite card. The legitimate-looking screen can therefore be promotional support for the engagement campaign rather than proof that the overall offer is trustworthy.

citations.quote: make sure you stop in on my mixer account.
Subscribed and commenting in the comments.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A creator may combine a genuine tutorial with ordinary channel promotion without that becoming a scam. The cited calls to action show audience-building, but they do not show impersonation, payment collection, credential theft, or a false redemption outcome. The tutorial's central instructions remain tied to signing in and entering the code, while the creator explicitly says the displayed card will not be redeemed by him.
